question: With the reclamation tick returning freed pages once a mount has shed its views and gone quiet, does G3 close?
answer: Yes. G3 is 13.3 / 16.1 / 16.3 MiB against a 256 MiB budget it was missing by 1.86 to 2.14x. The peak criterion does not close and is not addressed by this.
agreement_with_the_probe: The LD_PRELOAD interposer that first established the effect measured 10.2 / 12.4 / 14.2 MiB. The shipped tick lands at 13.3 / 16.1 / 16.3, so the mechanism reproduces in production code rather than only under a diagnostic.
what_does_not_close: traversed_with_old_files holds 492.8 / 490.7 / 504.1 MiB with 750,438 live views. Trimming returns pages after the fact; it cannot lower the high-water mark reached while the views were held. Whether the service runs on modest hardware turns on that peak, and only a resident bound lowers it.
consequence: G3 is now a hard assertion in the fixture: it passes, and a gate that passes and cannot fail is worth nothing. The peak criterion stays reporting until shedding lands, enforceable meanwhile through CIRROVE_CHURN_ENFORCE_MEMORY for anyone working on it.
limits: One run. The effect is two orders of magnitude beyond the 6 percent between-run variation of retained RSS, so this is not a close call, but the figures are not precise to three digits.
Zero-length files. No content mappings held.
Three attempts at the trim condition failed before this one, all invisible because firing could only be inferred. The allocator_trims counter now in every sample is what made the fourth verifiable.
